chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Jarmi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Durasht, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a group of people in Ihram who bought game and shared it, and a companion of theirs said to them, 'Make a share for me in it for one dirham,' so they made a share for her. He said: 'Upon each man among them is one sheep.'

key_terms.شَاةٌ: One sheep (the specific animal offered as fidya)
key_terms.صَيْداً: Game (hunted animals permissible to eat while in Ihram)
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation/Compensation (implied by the context of the ruling)
key_terms.مُحْرِمِينَ: People in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for men in Ihram who buy game for a woman?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the liability for expiation (kaffarah) in cases of accidental or shared hunting during Ihram is individual rather than collective, requiring each participant to offer one sheep. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the obligation of fidya attaches to the person who benefits from or participates in the prohibited act, even if the cost was shared. It highlights the precision in distinguishing between joint ownership and individual liability in ritual purity laws.
